retrieved_contexts:
['What is a token?
A token ≠ a word
A token is a piece of text, often a subword. This strategy makes it possible to 
handle rare words and various languages (Arabic, Darija, etc.).
Common word →  full token
Rare word →  split into subwords
Concrete example
The word "tokenization" becomes:
token
##ization', 'What information can other tokens 
OFFER?
Each token in the sequence doesn't just search — it also announces itself. It carries a kind of descriptive label that tells other tokens what it can 
bring them.
The token "river"
Announces: "I am a geographical/natural 
context. Useful if you're looking for a meaning 
related to water or terrain."
The token "credit"
Announces: "I am a financial/banking 
context. Useful if you're looking for a meaning 
related to money."
The token "the"
Announces: "I am a grammatical article. My 
semantic content is limited."
These "labels" are what we call the Keys — the second role of the attention mechanism.', 'Meaning depends on neighboring context
The tokens that surround a word determine its interpretation. This is not a hand-coded rule, but a statistical regularity that the model can learn.
🌊 Geographic context
« river », « water », « bank », « current » →  bank = natural riverbank
💶 Financial context
« account », « credit », « money », « loan » →  bank = financial 
institution
The solution: allow each token to look at its neighbors and adjust its representation accordingly.', 'tokens. Cross-attention weights [n_tgt, n_src] determine which source 
positions are most relevant for each target token. The encoder is NOT 
rerun — H is fixed throughout generation.
The encoder is run exactly once per source sentence. The decoder is run once per generated token, growing the target prefix by one 
token each step.', 'From Token to ID
The vocabulary = a dictionary
The tokenizer maintains an indexed list of all known tokens. Each 
token receives a unique numerical identifier — its index in this 
vocabulary.
This ID is the only "signal" passed to the next step.
Illustrative example
"The" → ID 42 "cat" → ID 4271
"eats" → ID 1587']
response: In NLP, a **token** is a piece of text—often a sub‑word—that the tokenizer splits the input into. Tokens can be whole words for common terms, but rare words are broken into smaller sub‑word units so the model can handle them and work across languages. For example, the word “tokenization” is split into the tokens “token” and “##ization”【Page 5】.
reference: A token is a piece of text, often a subword rather than a complete word. Tokenization lets a model process common and rare words, including across languages.
